activity_context.topic_title: Sums of Finite Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation

feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that we can rewrite the series as follows:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}\frac{20}{{5}^{n}}={\sum }_{n=1}^{4}20\cdot {(\frac{1}{5})}^{n}
$$

Since the above series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=\frac{1}{5}$ and $N=4.$ We need to figure out ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=20\cdot {(\frac{1}{5})}^{n},
$$

and therefore the first term of the series is

$$
{a}_{1}=20\cdot {(\frac{1}{5})}^{1}=4.
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=4$,  $r=\frac{1}{5}$ and $N=4$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}20\cdot {(\frac{1}{5})}^{n} & =4\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{5})}^{4}]}{(1-\frac{1}{5})} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{(1-\frac{1}{625})}{\frac{4}{5}} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{5}{4}\cdot \frac{624}{625} \\  & =\frac{624}{125}\end{aligned}
$$
